q: The network coding theorem (Ahlswede-Cai-Li-Yeung, 2000) for multicast networks states that the max-flow min-cut bound is:
opts: Achievable using linear network coding over a sufficiently large finite field
Only an upper bound, not achievable
exp: Ahlswede et al. proved the revolutionary result that for multicast (single source, multiple sinks), the max-flow min-cut capacity is achievable by allowing intermediate nodes to encode (mix) their received packets—linear network coding over GF(q) suffices for large enough q.
